prompts.prompt: How can a classifier get 95% accuracy and still miss every minority case?
sketch: Core: An imbalanced test set (e.g. 95 majority, 5 minority) with a classifier that predicts the majority for every case; accuracy (e.g. 95/100) and minority recall (e.g. 0/5) computed from the same counts.
Optional: A better metric to watch (recall, F1, balanced accuracy).

prompts.prompt: What does majority undersampling actually remove from the training set?
sketch: Core: The training rows before (e.g. six majority, two minority) and after (every minority row kept, a subset of majority rows kept), with the exact dropped majority row IDs named.
Optional: The test set left untouched; the information lost.

prompts.prompt: Why does recursive feature elimination refit after each drop?
sketch: Core: Feature scores at each fit; the lowest feature dropped, the survivors refitted and re-ranked (a ranking that changes after the refit, e.g. C overtaking B), repeated to the requested subset size, with feature identities tracked.
Optional: Why one fit's ranking would mislead (correlated features).

prompts.prompt: How do I calculate the population stability index one bin at a time?
sketch: Core: Reference and current shares on shared bins; each bin's term (current - reference) x ln(current / reference); an unchanged bin contributes 0; the terms summed to the PSI.
Optional: The usual thresholds (0.1, 0.25) and zero-share handling.
Core: An imbalanced training set; majority rows reduced to balance the classes while every minority row is kept; which rows are dropped.
Optional: The trade-off (lost majority information) and the contrast with oversampling.
